 Oral Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimants against the judgment and award dated 05.02.2021 passed by the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-XV,
Vijayapura [for short 'Tribunal'], in MVC No.315/2016, seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. One Dadarao met with an accident on 29.08.2015 and died.
His wife and children filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.11,75,000/- with interest.
The Tribunal considered the entire materials on record and awarded Rs.3,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the said order, claimants filed this appeal.

3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4.

The main contention of the claimants are that the income of the deceased was Rs.12,000/- per month by NC: 2025:KHC-K:6791 HC-KAR doing Agricultural work, but the Tribunal without any basis assessed the same at Rs.7,500/- per month and thus pray for enhancement of the compensation with 12% interest per annum instead of 6% awarded by the Tribunal.
5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper, which does not call for any interference.
6. Admittedly, at the time of accident deceased was aged 65 years and thus, the multiplier applicable is '7' and not '5' as taken by the Tribunal.
It is stated that he was earning Rs.12,000 per month, but no document is produced to prove the same.

In the absence of proof of income, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, this Court finds it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month for the accident of the year 2015,
instead of Rs.7,500/- as taken by the Tribunal.
If 1/3rd of this amount is deducted towards the personal expenses of NC: 2025:KHC-K:6791 HC-KAR the deceased, the claimants are entitled for 2/3rd of the income.

Thus, the loss of dependency comes to:
Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 7 x 2/3 = Rs.4,48,000/-.
7.

As per law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi claimant Nos.2 to 4 being children of the deceased are entitled for Rs.48,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium, in total Rs.1,44,000/- and also award an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads.
